facts.text: Qianmen Street stretches south from Tiananmen Square toward the old city wall, where imperial history and modern life share cobbles.
The gate that gives Qianmen its name, Zhengyangmen, was first built in 1419 during the Ming dynasty and once housed an archery tower.
Zhengyangmen survived the demolition of Beijing’s city walls in the 1960s, remaining the tallest gate at 42 metres high.
In 1900, the Boxer Rebellion saw the gate damaged when the Eight‑Nation Alliance invaded, marking a pivotal moment in Beijing’s modern history.
Qianmen’s first railway station, built just outside the gate, linked the city to the national network and later became a subway stop on Line 2.
A café in the historic Daguanlou building, once the birthplace of Chinese cinema, offers a taste of Beijing’s cultural past.
